specPoints.text: understand the nomenclature of alcohols and be able to draw their structural, displayed and skeletal formulae

primer.text: One hydroxyl group defines a family. This note fixes the alcohols' general formula, walks the alkan-ol naming rule through the first four members, and classifies primary, secondary and tertiary structures by counting the carbon neighbours of the carbon that carries the -OH.

lessons.title: The hydroxyl family: naming, formula and classes
sourceHeadings: The first four Alcohols and their Structures Table
lessons.opening: Alcohols are the family of organic compounds built around the hydroxyl group. This lesson fixes the general formula, walks the naming pattern, surveys the first four members, and classifies alcohols by how many carbon neighbours the hydroxyl carbon carries.
keyPoints: Alcohols contain the hydroxyl functional group -OH, and their general formula is CnH2n+1OH.
Naming follows the alkan-plus-ol pattern, giving methanol, ethanol, propan-1-ol and butan-1-ol for the first four members.
A molecule with two hydroxyl groups is called a diol.
Alcohols are classified primary, secondary or tertiary by how many other carbon atoms bond to the carbon carrying the -OH group.
Primary alcohols carry one carbon neighbour, secondary two, and tertiary three.

low.restatement: Count the carbons, add one hydroxyl, and the family formula CnH2n+1OH follows; the suffix -ol replaces -ane in the name, and the carbon bearing the -OH decides the class by counting its carbon neighbours.
low.analogy: A street of houses where every house has exactly one blue door: the door is the hydroxyl group, the street length is n, and how many neighbours share a fence with the blue-door house sets its class.
low.examPointer: Write the general formula and the alkan-ol naming rule together, and classify a given structure by counting the carbon atoms attached to the hydroxyl carbon.

medium.restatement: The hydroxyl group dominates the family's behaviour because the polar O-H bond anchors reactions at that carbon; the classification matters because primary, secondary and tertiary carbons oxidise differently later in the topic.
medium.analogy: The hydroxyl carbon is the family's front desk: visitors (reagents) always arrive there first, and how crowded the desk is with carbon neighbours decides what the desk can process.
medium.examPointer: When drawing structural, displayed or skeletal formulas, anchor the -OH first and the carbon counting becomes automatic.

check.stem: Which functional group defines an alcohol?

options.explanation: The family is defined by the polar hydroxyl group attached to a saturated carbon.
Carbonyls define aldehydes and ketones, not alcohols.
Carboxyl defines carboxylic acids, a different homologous series.
Halogen carriers are halogenoalkanes, not alcohols.

check.stem: The general formula of the alcohols is

options.explanation: Each extra carbon adds two hydrogens, plus the one in the hydroxyl, giving H2n+1.
That formula runs one hydrogen short for saturated alcohols.
That is the formula of an ether-like composition, not the alcohol series convention.
Hydrogen count grows with 2n+1, not with n.

check.stem: An alcohol whose -OH carbon is bonded to two other carbon atoms is classified as

options.explanation: Two carbon neighbours around the hydroxyl carbon define the secondary class.
Primary alcohols carry only one carbon neighbour.
Tertiary alcohols carry three carbon neighbours.

options.text: A diol, since two groups are involved
options.explanation: Diol counts hydroxyl groups per molecule, not carbon neighbours.

check.stem: Which name follows the alcohol naming convention correctly for a three-carbon chain with the hydroxyl on an end carbon?

options.explanation: The alkan-ol pattern with locant 1 places the hydroxyl on the first carbon of the propane chain.
The suffix drops the final e of the alkane name, giving propan-1-ol.
Numbering starts from the end nearer the hydroxyl, so locant 3 is wrong for an end carbon.
The systematic convention is the -ol suffix with a locant, not this form.

check.stem: A molecule containing two -OH groups on different carbons is called

options.explanation: Two hydroxyl groups on one molecule make a diol by definition.
Classification by carbon neighbours is separate from counting hydroxyl groups.
Hydrates are water-containing solids, not covalent molecules with two -OH groups.
Peroxides contain an O-O bond, which a diol need not have.

check.stem: State the general formula of the alcohols.
check.modelAnswer: The alcohols have the general formula CnH2n+1OH, one hydroxyl group per formula unit.

check.stem: Name the first four members of the alcohol series.
check.modelAnswer: Methanol, ethanol, propan-1-ol and butan-1-ol, with one, two, three and four carbons respectively.

check.stem: Explain why ethanol is classified as a primary alcohol.
check.modelAnswer: In ethanol the carbon carrying the hydroxyl group is bonded to only one other carbon atom, the methyl carbon, and one carbon neighbour is precisely the definition of a primary alcohol.

check.stem: Classify butan-2-ol and justify the class from its carbon framework.
check.modelAnswer: Butan-2-ol is secondary: the hydroxyl sits on carbon 2 of the butane chain, and that carbon is bonded to two other carbon atoms, carbons 1 and 3 of the chain.

glossary.definition: The -OH functional group that defines the alcohols and anchors their characteristic reactions.
An alcohol whose hydroxyl-bearing carbon is bonded to exactly one other carbon atom.
An alcohol whose hydroxyl-bearing carbon is bonded to two other carbon atoms.
An alcohol whose hydroxyl-bearing carbon is bonded to three other carbon atoms.
A molecule carrying two hydroxyl groups.

workedExample.prompt: Use the general formula CnH2n+1OH to obtain the molecular formula of ethanol and its molar mass.
steps: Ethanol has two carbon atoms, so set n = 2.
The hydrogen count follows from the formula: 2n + 1 = 2 x 2 + 1 = 5, giving C2H5OH.
Add the molar masses: 2 x 12.0 for carbon, 5 x 1.0 for the chain hydrogens, plus 17.0 for the OH group, totalling 46.0.
Check the count against the structure: two carbons, five chain hydrogens and one hydroxyl match the drawn molecule exactly.
workedExample.finalAnswer: Ethanol is C2H5OH with a molar mass of 46.0 g mol-1.
